question.text: Which category of Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs) can be either open-ended or closed-ended as per SEBI regulations?

answer.text: All categories of AIFs must be closed-ended

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the NISM Series II-A workbook (page 47), Category I and Category II AIFs are close-ended funds, while only Category III AIFs can be either open-ended or close-ended. The Trap: Option D sounds plausible because Categories I and II are close-ended, but Category III is the exception, so a blanket "all AIFs are close-ended" rule is incorrect. Note: Memorise the page 47 distinction: Categories I and II are close-ended; Category III is either open-ended or close-ended.
